articles.title: Puka Nacua injury update: Rams star wideout expected to be a game-time decision, but is reportedly 'trending in the wrong direction' due to hip and groin injuries
articles.summary: Puka Nacua did not practice Friday or Saturday due to hip and groin issues.
articles.body:
Coming off a surprising loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Los Angeles Rams need to bounce back against the New York Giants in Week 2 to live up to their status as Super Bowl contenders. But that task could prove difficult, as star wideout Puka Nacua will reportedly be a game-time decision who is " trending in the wrong direction " for Monday's game due to hip and groin injuries, per ESPN.

After a modest performance in the team's 27-7 loss to the 49ers, in which he caught five passes for 74 yards, Nacua was able to get on the practice field Thursday. But the wideout unexpectedly did not practice Friday, with head coach Sean McVay saying Nacua "didn't feel totally like himself" during Thursday's practice. The Rams eventually listed Nacua on the team's injury report with a hip issue.

After Nacua failed to practice Saturday, McVay added another ailment to the list, saying Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" to his groin, per ESPN. Despite not practicing both days, Nacua was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report.

While a questionable designation often results in a player trying to gut it out, McVay said Saturday that Nacua would be a true game-time decision in Week 2, per ESPN.

"Whether or not he plays is to be determined," McVay said. "And so we'll see how he's feeling."

It's a concerning development for Nacua, who — on top of playing Monday night — already had additional days to recover following the team's Week 1 game against the 49ers. That game aired Thursday night in the United States, giving Nacua a full 10 days to rest up for Week 2.

When healthy, Nacua is considered one of the best receivers in football. After gaining 1,715 receiving yards and scoring 10 touchdowns last season, Nacua was named a first-team All-Pro for the first time in his career.

The 25-year-old has battled minor injuries and ailments since being drafted in 2023. A knee issue caused Nacua to miss five games in 2024 and an ankle issue forced him to miss a game last season. He's popped up on the injury report other times, but has usually played through issues.

Who would replace Puka Nacua for Rams in Week 2?

If Nacua is unable to go in Week 1, veteran Davante Adams would serve as the team's de-facto No. 1 option against the Giants. Jordan Whittingham and Tutu Atwell could also see increased snaps if Nacua is out. The team could also feature tight end Terrance Ferguson more as a pass catcher if Nacua is unable to do his usual middle-of-the-field work.

Regardless of Nacua's status, the Rams need to turn in a much better performance in Week 2. After a listless outing in Week 1, the Rams can't afford to open the year 0-2, not when the team entered the year as one of the Super Bowl favorites.

articles.title: From a $15M divorce to a secret newborn at 54: Michael Strahan has everything except a reason to ever get married again
articles.summary: NFL News: Michael Strahan’s personal life has taken another turn at 54. The former NFL star and *Good Morning America* co-anchor is now a father of five after r.
articles.body: Michael Strahan’s personal life has taken another turn at 54. The former NFL star and *Good Morning America* co-anchor is now a father of five after reportedly welcoming a baby girl with longtime girlfriend Kayla Quick earlier this year. The news came weeks before Strahan opened up about marriage and admitted he is unsure about walking down the aisle again. After two marriages, a broken engagement and a costly divorce involving Jean Muggli, Strahan says he still believes in love, but his latest comments suggest marriage is no longer something he feels he needs to pursue.Why is Michael Strahan unsure about getting married again?Michael Strahan was asked directly about marriage during a recent interview with *Playboy*, and his answer was hardly a firm yes or no.“Would I get married again? Let’s not go there,” he joked during the interview. “Why you gonna put me on the spot like that?”He then left the door open without suggesting he was actively planning another wedding.“I’ll never say never,” continued Strahan. “I love love. Sometimes love doesn’t love me back.”The comments carry more weight given his history. Strahan has been married twice. His first marriage, to Wanda Hutchins, lasted from 1992 to 1996. He later married Jean Muggli in 1999, with the couple eventually divorcing in 2006. He was also engaged to Nicole Murphy, with that relationship ending in 2014. PEOPLE reported at the time that distance and demanding work schedules contributed to their split.What happened in Michael Strahan’s $15 million divorce?Strahan’s divorce from Muggli became one of the most expensive chapters of his personal life. In 2007, a judge awarded Muggli a reported $15 million divorce settlement, with Strahan also ordered to pay $18,000 a month in child support. Some later reports put the settlement at $15.3 million.The former couple share twin daughters, Isabella and Sophia, who are now 21. Strahan also has two older children, Tanita and Michael Jr., from his first marriage to Hutchins.That history helps explain why marriage may not carry the same appeal for him today. Still, Strahan has not said that he has rejected marriage permanently. His own words are more measured. He says he loves love and refuses to completely close the door.Who is Michael Strahan’s girlfriend Kayla Quick?Strahan has been linked to Kayla Quick since 2015, but the couple has kept much of their relationship away from public view. They rarely appear together and have not publicly detailed how they first met. Quick is also a co-founder of wellness company FIZZNESS.In August, PEOPLE reported that Strahan and Quick had welcomed their first child together. TMZ was first to report that the baby girl was born earlier in 2026. That made her Strahan’s fifth child.The timing makes his marriage comments particularly interesting, but there is no indication from Strahan that becoming a father again has changed his view of marriage.For now, his priorities appear to be family, work and the life he has built outside the NFL. Strahan has previously spoken about feeling happy and fortunate with the people around him. At 54, he does not appear eager to force his personal life into a familiar script just because marriage is expected to be the next step.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Colts WR Keenan Allen facing at least a 3-game suspension following August drunk-driving arrest
articles.summary: The 34-year-old is expected to still play in Sunday night's game against the Chiefs.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was charged this week with two misdemeanor offenses stemming from his drunk-driving arrest on August 30.

A violation of the league's substance-abuse policy, which this was, comes with a minimum three-game suspension under the current NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement. A longer suspension can be issued if the player was more intoxicated.

Allen blew a .224 when he was arrested, nearly triple the legal limit of .08. His blood alcohol level was so high that it actually triggered a more serious Class A misdemeanor according to Indiana law.

The NFL is reportedly waiting for the legal proceedings of the case to conclude before issuing a suspension. Allen and the Colts will play the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2's "Sunday Night Football" game, despite the looming suspension.

The next aspect of Allen's case is expected to be an attorney conference on Oct. 26. This would mean that, at the earliest, the wide receiver's suspension could begin in Week 8 if the NFL does indeed wait for the situation to play out in the legal system.

The 34-year-old veteran was arrested at the end of August. He was initially charged with "operating a vehicle with alcohol concentration equivalent to .15 or more, and operating a vehicle while intoxicated." Both of these charges are misdemeanors.

Allen joined the Colts on a one-year deal. In his debut with the team in Week 1, he came down with all six of his targets for 32 yards.

The veteran wide receiver spent the 2025 season with the Los Angeles Chargers . Allen began his career with the franchise and played 11 years in San Diego and L.A. before leaving for the Chicago Bears for the 2024 season.

In 172 career games, Allen has tallied 12,083 yards with 70 touchdowns. He was expected to add a veteran presence to the Colts' receiving corps alongside Alec Pierce and Josh Downs . Now, Indianapolis awaits to see when, and for how long, it will lose Allen to a suspension.

articles.title: Steelers want Joey Porter Jr. to return in Week 3, but cornerback reportedly still struggling with back injury
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr. will miss at least two games as he ramps back up after missing most of training camp.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers picked up a win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1 despite missing one of the team's most important defensive players. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. sat out for that contest due to back and conditioning issues. While Porter participated in limited practices in Week 2, he'll miss Sunday's contest at the New England Patriots due to those issues.

If the team has its way, Porter will take the field next week. The Steelers are reportedly planning for Porter to return to action against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3.

Whether Porter actually takes the field, however, is an open question … both due to his back injury and — possibly — his contract situation, per ESPN .

But whether or not Porter actually does return is a bit more ambiguous and is connected to the star cornerback's back injury and conditioning level. Porter's back, according to a source, has "flared up when he's tried to go full speed, and they haven't been able to get it where it needs to be." Porter has been considering getting a second opinion on his back.

But whether or not Porter actually does return is a bit more ambiguous and is connected to the star cornerback's back injury and conditioning level.

Porter's back, according to a source, has "flared up when he's tried to go full speed, and they haven't been able to get it where it needs to be." Porter has been considering getting a second opinion on his back.

Porter — who is in the final year of his rookie contract — missed time early in training camp due to the situation. While he was able to return to practices ahead of the regular season, Porter was deemed to be in a "ramp-up" situation thanks to a back injury and his conditioning.

Despite practicing in a limited capacity each day leading up to Week 1, Porter did not play in the contest. Similarly, Porter was able to get in limited practice ahead of Week 2. This time around, however, the team ruled him out on its final injury report. That wasn't the case ahead of Week 1, when Porter was listed as "questionable" on the final injury report.

It's unclear when or how the situation will resolve itself. If Porter is truly plagued by a back issue, then the cornerback could miss additional weeks recovering from the injury. If his continued absences are related to Porter's contract situation, that could also cause issues, as the team has a long-standing policy of not negotiating contracts during the regular season.

If the team changes its mind, the framework for a deal is fairly obvious. In early September, the New England Patriots and cornerback Christian Gonzalez agreed to a four-year, $135 million extension that made Gonzalez the highest-paid cornerback in the league. Porter would — almost certainly — look to match or exceed that figure with his next contract.

Should Porter continue to sit out, a trade could wind up being the most likely outcome. The Steelers have reportedly entertained the idea, but are seeking a first-round pick in the deal, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor. That ask has reportedly scared teams off.

Porter's price could fall the longer the cornerback misses time. If that's the case, a trade could wind up being the best thing for both sides.

That scenario could potentially be avoided if Porter's back is OK and he returns to action in Week 3. That makes the upcoming week a big deal for both sides.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers NFL Week 2 Live Updates, Highlights and Analysis
articles.summary: After getting drilled by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, the Cleveland Browns are still in Florida. Sunday, the Browns will take on a familiar face in Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
After getting drilled by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, the Cleveland Browns are still in Florida. Sunday, the Browns will take on a familiar face in Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The game is more than just the embodiment of the Deshaun Watson debacle. It's a make-or-break for Watson if he wants to remain the starter in Cleveland. An opportunity for the Browns to either shake off the stink of last week's beatdown or confirm the opinions of so many that the Browns are (again) among the worst teams in the NFL.

We won't get into which one this analyst thinks will happen—there will be plenty of time to be depressed once the game kicks off.

Once it does, keep it here at Bleacher Report for highlights and commentary as the Browns try to salvage a split from their Florida road trip.

And as Watson tries to salvage his career—because that's where we are.

Well, while we twiddle our thumbs, might as well take a quick tour of the division.

The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-0 for the second straight year after going to Houston and beating the Texans 20-6. The Bengals were outgained by over 100 yards, but Cincy's new-look defense kept Houston out of the end zone.

The Baltimore Ravens, on the other hand, were stunned at home by the New Orleans Saints 24-17. Baltimore's defense just couldn't get stops when they needed, allowing the Saints to convert eight-of-15 third downs.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are similarly 1-1 after a listless 20-3 loss at New England. Pittsburgh managed just 235 yards of offense, and the Steelers now have one offensive touchdown in two games.

A weather delay is a pain in the rear end.

Scoring three points in the muck one week after piling up 59 points and losing your starting quarterback indefinitely is beyond brutal.

Regardless of how this game plays out, the Deshaun Watson decision just became a lot harder for Todd Monken.

If Cleveland hangs on for the win, it would be difficult for Monken to justify making a change. Watson's effort against the Buccaneers is one of his best as a member off the Browns—30 attempts, 24 completions, 238 yards and a passer rating above 120. He looked like an NFL starter.

If the Browns falter, fans will likely clamor for Shedeur Sanders. A large percentage of the fanbase wants no part of Watson no way no how. But Sanders has never looked as good over an entire game as Watson did in Tampa.

In this analyst's opinion, Watson has earned another start.

With that said, it's not my decision to make—and there's going to be 67,000 fans eager to voice their opinion on the subject next Sunday.

This may actually be a blessing in disguise for the Browns--the Buccaneers were moving downfield with relative ease.

Yes, you read that right. Don't be alarmed. This probably doesn't mean it's the Apocalypse.

The Browns just had far and away their best drive of the 2026 campaign--12 plays, 68 yards, multiple third-down conversions and a 17-yard touchdown pass from Watson to Blake "Who?" Whiteheart.

The Browns have their first lead of the season.

The Browns appear to have found themselves a player in second-round rookie Denzel Boston. The former Washington standout has five catches for 95 yards and a score for the second straight week.

A 49-yard pass from Baker Mayfield to Tez Johnson left the Buccaneers knocking on the door, but as has been the case most of this game Cleveland's defense stiffened, forcing another Chase McLaughlin field goal.

With 10 minutes to play, the Browns are still in it.

OK, so maybe I spoke too soon about the whole "one touchdown" thing.

The Browns actually have two for the season--both on long catches by Denzel Boston.

The second one admittedly had as much to do with terrible tackling by Tampa as the throw or catch.

But six points are six points--and we have ourselves a ballgame.

To be fair, Cleveland's offense had their best drive of the game after Tampa scored a touchdown--and it took an excellent defensive play to prevent rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston from hauling in a touchdown pass.

But the NFL is a results business--and seven quarters in the Browns have one offensive touchdown.

This was the nightmare scenario for the Browns--gifting Tampa a field goal just before the half and then watching the Buccaneers drive the length of the field to open the second half.

Cleveland is all about nightmares though, so that's exactly what happened--nine plays, 65 yards and a five-yard pass from Baker Mayfield to Emeka Egbuka.

In the first half against the Buccaneers, the Browns had 59 yards of offense--and 50 yards in penalties.

He's 6'4". 260 pounds. 25 years old. Answers to the name Jared Verse.

Part of the Myles Garrett trade, Verse was supposed to help soften the blow of Garrett's departure. Be an instant contributor for the Browns defensively.

Instead, Verse has been invisible--although he did get his first pressure of the season in the first half against Tampa.

That's right. Six quarters. One pressure.

Credit to the Browns for holding the Buccaneers to a field goal attempt after Todd Monken gifted them a short field. But Chase McLaughlin's field goal just before the half gives Tampa a 9-6 lead at the break.

90 minutes into the 2026 season, the Browns have led for exactly as much time as Browns fans have been happy.

A lack of situational awareness from rookie wideout KC Concepcion.

A lack of intelligence from head coach Todd Monken, who went for it on fourth-and-one from their own 35-yard line.

A complete lack of push from the offensive line.

After the Browns traded the second overall pick in 2025 to the Jaguars, the team used the fifth overall pick on Michigan defensive tackle Mason Graham.

Graham was quiet statistically as a rookie, but he's taken it up a notch in 2026. His second quarter sack of Baker Mayfield was his second in as many games.

The Browns have a lack of discipline that would be funny if it wasn't so sad.

Another holding penalty put Cleveland in first-and-20. Then Watson got sacked (again) by Keionte Scott.

Just over halfway through the second quarter, Cleveland has 51 yards of offense.

The Browns got Tampa behind the sticks. Third and 18. And then promptly surrendered a 21-yard pass to rookie receiver Ted Hurst.

However, the Browns are also doing a far better job pressuring Mayfield than in Week 1, and a Ronnie Hickman sack forced the Buccaneers to punt.

This Browns team is absolutely maddening.

After the Harden interception gave the Browns excellent field position, Cleveland was moving the ball. But yet another penalty put Cleveland behind the sticks, Deshaun Watson was dropped by David Walker on third and long and the Browns had to settle for three again.

The penalties are inexcusable--and a sign of bad coaching.

Great job by young defensive back Myles harden of reading Baker Mayfield's eyes and picking off a pass that puts the Browns in business in Tampa territory.

Well, at least they aren't allowing touchdowns.

A 30-yard Bucky Irving run got Tampa into scoring range, but the Cleveland defense stiffened and the Buccaneers were once again forced to settle for a Chase McLaughlin field goal.

That's two scores in as many drives though.

The good news is that the Browns showed more life on their second drive than in the entire first half against Jacksonville, driving 40 yards in seven plays before a 50-yard Andre Szymt field goal tied the game.

The bad news is that the Browns were forced to settle for three after yet another pre-snap penalty.

Still, Cleveland answered Tampa's drive.

There's admittedly not a lot that a team can do when a kicker hits from 59 yards out.

But the Browns let their opponent score on their opening drive--again. And now Cleveland is in an early hole--again.

Three Cleveland penalties in the first two minutes of the game.

That's after 11 last week against the Jags.

To be fair, when the Browns moved on from Mayfield it was time. His level of play had stagnated, and he didn't handle the news that the team was going to pursue Deshaun Watson especially well.

But that doesn't make what has happened since any easier to stomach.

Deshaun Watson's raw stats last week against the Jaguars weren't terrible. But for once numbers do lie--Watson didn't play well and those stats were buoyed by a garbage-time TD.

Per Ian Rapoport of ESPN , the Browns plan to "re-evaluate" their quarterback situation after Week 2.

I'll save them the trouble. It stinks. Watson stinks. And when Shedeur Sanders inevitably gets the nod, he'll stink.

But unless Watson lights up the Buccaneers, the Browns cannot start him in the home opener against the Carolina Panthers.

Browns fans will--let's put it this way.

As a group, they have been known to throw things.

articles.title: How Gisele Bündchen walking away became the defining moment of Tom Brady's final and most painful NFL season
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady spent 23 years outrunning pressure, reading defenses, and delivering in the moments that mattered most. But during a recent appearance on Fo.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent 23 years outrunning pressure, reading defenses, and delivering in the moments that mattered most. But during a recent appearance on Fox Sports' The Herd, the seven-time Super Bowl champion admitted something no highlight reel ever captured: his 2022 season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the last of his career, was shaped far more by what was happening at home than anything that unfolded on the field. His marriage to Gisele Bündchen was falling apart. Publicly. Painfully. Right in the middle of a season he couldn't walk away from.Why did Tom Brady's divorce from Gisele Bündchen affect his performance on the field?There's a reason the 2022 season felt different. Tom Brady posted an 8-9 record that year, the only losing season of his entire career. Statistically, he still threw for 4,694 yards with 25 touchdowns. The numbers weren't embarrassing. But anyone who watched closely knew something was off.Gisele Bündchen had made her feelings about his return to the NFL very clear. After Brady announced his retirement in February 2022, only to reverse that decision weeks later, reports emerged that she was deeply unhappy about it. By October, the divorce was official. She filed. He kept playing. And every Sunday, Brady was suiting up for the Buccaneers while his 13-year marriage was dissolving in the tabloids and courtrooms."My last season was tough," Brady told The Herd. "I was going through — I had a lot of, you know, just a personal, family issue, and it was a challenge. It was very ... it just took a lot out of me in terms of, you know, my ability to continue to play."That's about as candid as Brady gets.Did Tom Brady's decision to un-retire cost him his marriage to Gisele Bündchen?It's hard to say it was one decision alone, but the unretirement certainly lit the fuse. Bündchen had reportedly grown frustrated with football for years, not just the time it consumed but the physical toll it was taking. She shared publicly that she worried about his long-term health. Two children at home. A life she wanted him to be present for.When Brady walked back his retirement, it sent a clear signal about where his priorities still sat. Their separation quietly began during preseason. Brady took a mysterious 10-day leave from Buccaneers training camp that August and nobody explained why. He later hinted at personal struggles. By the time October came, the divorce was filed and confirmed.He was 45, playing in his 23rd NFL season, while the marriage he had built over 13 years was ending. That is not a small thing to carry into a huddle on a Sunday afternoon.What did Tom Brady say about his regrets and moving on after the Gisele Bündchen divorce?Brady didn't dwell in self-pity during his comments on The Herd. If anything, he framed it with the same controlled restraint he brought to every fourth quarter he ever played. He acknowledged the difficulty but didn't point fingers or assign blame."I felt like I always had a goal — 45," he said. "I was 45 years old, I wanted to spend time with my kids. I felt like, okay, now it's time for me to be at all my kids' games. They've been to enough of their dad's games."He and Bündchen share two children together, Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. Brady also has an 18-year-old son, Jack, from his previous relationship with actress Bridget Moynihan. The divorce was finalized amicably, with both issuing statements about co-parenting and moving forward.But reading between the lines of what he said on The Herd, there's an honest reckoning there. Brady chose one more season of football. It cost him his marriage. And now, three years removed from all of it, he's saying out loud what most people already suspected: that 2022 broke him in ways the NFL never did.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ernie Accorsi — former Giants GM who set up team to win two Super Bowls — dead at 84
articles.summary: Ernie Accorsi was inducted into the Giants' Ring of Honor in 2016.
articles.body:
Ernie Accorsi — a football-lifer who helped the New York Giants win two Super Bowls — died Saturday, the team announced . He was 84.

In a statement, Giants president John Mara called Accorsi a "trusted advisor and dear friend."

"Ernie helped shape the course of New York Giants history through his vision, leadership and unwavering belief in building a championship organization. Beyond his accomplishments as a football executive, he was a trusted advisor and dear friend. His legacy will forever be part of the Giants, and he will be greatly missed."

While Accorsi's NFL journey began back in 1970, his biggest contributions to the game came as a member of the Giants. Accorsi initially joined the team as an assistant to the general manager before being promoted into the GM role in 1998.

The team reached the Super Bowl during the 2000 NFL season, where it fell to the Baltimore Ravens .

Following that loss, Accorsi was instrumental in building the Giants team that would eventually go on to win two Super Bowl titles. Between 2000 and 2006 — the year he retired — Accorsi acquired Eli Manning , Jeremy Shockey, Osi Umenyiora , Justin Tuck , Brandon Jacobs and Plaxico Burress through the draft, trades or free agency. All six of those players would play key roles in the team winning the Super Bowl during the 2007 and 2011 seasons.

Though Accorsi set up the majority of the roster that won it all in 2007, he was not technically a member of the Giants that season due to his retirement. The team, however, awarded Accorsi a championship ring for being the architect that brought that group together.

In 2016, the Giants honored Accorsi by inducting him into the team's Ring of Honor. Accorsi was inducted alongside Tuck and head coach Tom Coughlin — another member of the franchise who was recruited by Accorsi.

While all of those acquisitions played a massive role in the team's two Super Bowl wins, it was Accorsi's trade for Manning that stands above the rest. Entering the 2004 NFL Draft, Manning, Philip Rivers and Ben Roethlisberger were thought to be the three top quarterbacks in the draft. While Manning was expected to be the No. 1 overall pick, he did not want to play for the then-San Diego Chargers. Despite his pleas, the Chargers selected Manning No. 1 overall. It was initially unclear whether the team would force the issue or trade Manning away.

It didn't take long before that question was answered. The Giants — which picked No. 4 — grabbed Rivers moments later, and then agreed to swap the quarterbacks in a deal that shaped the future of multiple NFL franchises.

While both players put up excellent numbers over their careers, Manning led the Giants to two Super Bowl titles. Rivers never won a Super Bowl in his 18 years in the NFL. Both players, however, have a shot to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the future.

Manning also released a statement, thanking Accorsi for "making the trade and believing in me."

Coughlin, similarly, highlighted the Manning trade as Accorsi's biggest move.

"Ernie will always be remembered, and I say this out of great respect, he's the guy that made the trade for Eli Manning. That will go down in Giants history as one of the great moves of all time. Was it risky? Sure it was risky. Ernie did it. Shut the door, went in, he did it on his own. It was his move. He had followed Eli from the time Eli was a very young player at Ole Miss, and he was convinced that Eli was the franchise quarterback that the Giants needed. He was not going to be deterred. He saw an opportunity. I think both teams benefitted greatly from the decision, and Ernie pulled the trigger."

Ernie Accorsi spent decades working in football

Prior to joining the Giants, Accorsi served as the general manager of the Cleveland Browns , where he is credited for bringing franchise icon Bernie Kosar to the team. Prior to that, he was the general manager of the Baltimore Colts, and oversaw the team selecting — and then trading — John Elway. While Accorsi was the team's general manager at the time of that trade, it was team owner Jim Irsay — and not Accorsi — who was credited with trading Elway away.

Following his retirement from the Giants, Accorsi served as a consultant with a number of NFL teams, often assisting when those teams were looking for new general managers or coaches.

articles.title: Packers WR Jayden Reed leaves field on backboard with his neck stabilized after contact to head on tackle
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed left the field on a cart with his head stabilized after a frightening scene during Sunday's game against the New...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed left the field on a cart with his head stabilized after a frightening scene during Sunday's game against the New York Jets .

The Packers quickly ruled him out with a neck injury.

Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele also left in the first quarter with a knee injury and was ruled out. The precise nature of Bako-Bewele's injury wasn't initially clear.

Reed carted off after being placed on backboard

Jets linebacker Demario Davis made contact to Reed's head with his shoulder pad on a hit in the first quarter. Reed was face down on the ground for a moment before rolling over to his back.

Medical staff immediately tended to Reed, and Packers players left their bench to surround their injured teammate as a cart came out.

Trainers put Reed on a backboard and stabilized his head before placing him on a cart. Reed was then taken off the field on the cart.

The precise nature and extent of Reed's injury weren't initially clear.

Reed, 26, is a fourth-year pro who's played his entire career for the Packers since being selected in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He's the No. 2 receiver on Green Bay 's depth chart behind Christian Watson .

Collarbone and foot injuries limited Reed to seven games in 2025. In his last full NFL season in 2024, Reed tallied 55 catches for 857 yards and 6 touchdowns. He posted three catches for 20 yards in Green Bay's Week 1 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .

articles.title: Ja'Marr Chase's first TD of the NFL season was sensational
articles.summary: Ja'Marr Chase got off to a slow start in Week 1 with just 2 catches for 12 yards. He'll be at the top of the highlight reels for Week 2.
articles.body:
Ja'Marr Chase got off to a slow start in Week 1 with just two catches for 12 yards. He'll be at the top of the highlight reels for Week 2.

With the Bengals locked in a scoreless tie late in the first half against the Houston Texans , Chase got Cincinnati on the board in spectacular fashion.

On first-and-10 from the Houston 32-yard line, Chase ran a go route down the right sideline. Texans cornerback Derek Stingley had tight man coverage on Chase, but no help over the top.

Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow didn't hesitate to look Chase's way. He uncorked a deep pass toward the end zone.

Chase got just enough separation from Stingley as he tracked the ball, then turned around and snagged the ball out of the air, narrowly getting both feet down just inside the pylon. He secured possession with his right foot down, then got his left down in the end zone, just barely inbounds as he fell out of bounds.

Both of his feet were down as he had possession of the ball, and the Bengals struck first on the scoreboard for a 7-0 lead.

Chase is coming off a second consecutive season with 125-plus receptions that earned him his fifth Pro Bowl nod and third-career All-Pro selection. His slow start in Week 1 was notable, but no real reason for concern. As long as he's healthy, Chase remains one of the game's best receivers and most dangerous offensive weapons.

articles.summary: Saquon Barkley was injured after just one carry in Week 2, but returned in the third quarter.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles had a rough first drive against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Things started off ominously, as star running back Saquon Barkley left the contest after just one carry due to a stinger.

After being tackled on the first carry of the game, Barkley went into the medical tent on the sideline and eventually jogged to the locker room.

He was initially deemed questionable to return due to a stinger and missed the rest of the first half due to the injury. But when the third quarter began, Barkley was back out on the field.

Things only got worse during the Eagles first drive, as quarterback Jalen Hurts threw an interception with the Eagles on the 8-yard line.

That interception was returned all the way to the opposing 10-yard line, setting up the Titans to score a touchdown a few plays later to take an early 7-0 lead.

Philadelphia battled back without Barkley in the first half, taking a 14-10 lead into halftime.

articles.title: Cooper Rush Benched for Jack Strand During Falcons vs. Panthers After 5 Turnovers in 2 Games
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons were forced to make another change at quarterback after another disappointing showing from Cooper Rush.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons were forced to make another change at quarterback after another disappointing showing from Cooper Rush.

After throwing two interceptions and losing a fumble in Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers, Rush was benched in the third quarter for rookie signal-caller Jack Strand. Fans at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta erupted after the quarterback change:

Unfortunately, it was more of the same for Atlanta as Strand's first pass was an interception returned for a touchdown:

The Falcons were planning on having Tua Tagovailoa open the year as their starting quarterback, but an oblique injury has kept him sidelined for the past two weeks. With third-year signal-caller Michael Penix Jr. continuing his recovery from a partially torn ACL, Atlanta was left to turn to Rush.

However, Rush's first start was far from effective, as he threw two interceptions in a 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. He completed just 12 of his 22 passes and sustained four sacks.

Sunday's start against Carolina wasn't any better, as the nine-year veteran went 10-of-17 for 86 yards before being benched. Without an effective passing attack, star running back Bijan Robinson hasn't been able to get much going on the ground.

The Falcons appear to be on their way to their first 0-2 start since the 2022 season, but help could be on the way. ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported that Penix could be cleared to play against the Green Bay Packers in Week 3. After Rush's disappointing showing and Strand's rough start, it's clear that Atlanta needs more stability under center to be competitive this year.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Injured, Latest on Bears Star After Being Carted Off in Vikings Loss
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears' season may have just taken a very concerning turn.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears' season may have just taken a very concerning turn.

Franchise quarterback Caleb Williams appeared to suffer a serious leg injury during Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings while scrambling from the pocket. He was later rul ed out with a hamstring injury.

Head coach Ben Johnson provided an update after the game:

Williams is heading into his third season with the Bears after leading his team to an NFC North title and the divisional round of the playoffs in 2025.

He completed 58.1 percent of his passes last season for 3,942 yards with 27 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Williams also added 77 carries for 388 rushing yards and three touchdowns while leading the Bears to an 11-6 record.

Although he took significantly fewer sacks during his sophomore campaign, going from a historic 68 sacks as rookie to 24 sacks last season, Williams also saw his completion percentage drop.

Bears coach Ben Johnson made improving Williams' accuracy a focus during training camp this offseason.

Taking that step forward this fall will require a healthy Williams. If he is sidelined for any length of time, however, the Bears will turn to Case Keenum in the short term.

articles.title: Patriots Beat Steelers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Aaron Rodgers, Maye, DK, Top Players
articles.summary: After starting the year with a loss to the Seattle Seahawks, the New England Patriots got back on track with a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.
articles.body:
After starting the year with a loss to the Seattle Seahawks, the New England Patriots got back on track with a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday.

The Patriots, who were 16.5-point favorites over the Steelers (via FanDuel Sportsbook ), cruised past Pittsburgh 20-3 at home.

After missing Week 1 against the Seahawks, Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson had a nice start to his season, scoring on New England's second drive of the game on a 39-yard rush.

After Henderson's score, both offenses had a slow first half, with each picking up a field goal before halftime. The Steelers appeared to have some momentum early in the third quarter when they intercepted Drake Maye on the first drive of the half, but they couldn't capitalize and had to punt.

The Patriots took a 13-3 lead with a field goal late in the third quarter and then forced an Aaron Rodgers fumble that resulted in a touchdown to make it 20-3 early in the fourth.

The mistakes from Rodgers continued later in the fourth when he threw an interception in the red zone.

While New England couldn't capitalize on the pick, it essentially sealed the win for the Pats since they were able to run the clock down and leave the Steelers with just over three minutes to mount a comeback.

The Patriots looked questionable in their season opener last week, and there is clearly still plenty to work on, but a double-digit win is a good way to get back on track ahead of a tough stretch against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills.

The Steelers won their season opener against the Atlanta Falcons, but a dreadful performance on Sunday will likely have fans questioning whether Rodgers and new head coach Mike McCarthy can get Pittsburgh to the playoffs.

articles.title: Vikings Beat Bears Amid Caleb Williams Injury, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Jefferson, More
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears lost Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Minnesota Vikings 9-3, but that was the least of their concern.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears lost Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Minnesota Vikings 9-3, but that was the least of their concern.

Franchise quarterback Caleb Williams suffered a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room in front of a stunned Soldier Field crowd in the fourth quarter. Backup Tyson Bagent entered in his place, Minnesota blocked the ensuing field goal that would have tied the game and it felt like the season was already slipping away for the Bears.

Bagent had a chance to be a hero on the final possession, but he took a sack on the last snap.

On the other side, Carson Wentz, Aaron Jones and Justin Jefferson made just enough plays to get the victory with the Minnesota defense playing at such a high level.

It was reasonable to expect offensive fireworks in this one considering the Bears and Carolina Panthers combined for 96 points in Week 1 while the Vikings and Green Bay Packers combined for 61.

However, the rainy conditions and defenses had other plans.

Minnesota took a 6-3 lead into halftime as neither offense generated any momentum in the subpar weather. Williams threw an interception to Byron Murphy Jr., Wentz had a completion percentage below 50 percent at intermission and the defenses were in full control as both sides combined for five first-half punts.

It seemed like Chicago was finally going to get into the end zone on the opening possession of the second half when Williams scrambled around and found Kalif Raymond, but D'Andre Swift lost a fumble at the Minnesota 1-yard line.

The turnover was a brief respite from the punt fest, which returned for the rest of the third quarter as both offenses continued to stall in the conditions.

Unfortunately for the Bears, that fumble was just a hint at the pain that was yet to come.

They once again moved inside the Minnesota 10-yard line in the fourth quarter behind completions to Swift and Rome Odunze. However, Williams suffered the injury when he was running toward the end zone on a possession that ended in a blocked Cairo Santos field goal.

The field goal would have come in handy when the Bears again moved into the red zone on the last possession, as they took a sack as time expired.

Minnesota will look to continue building momentum when it faces the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3, while Chicago will host the Philadelphia Eagles as it attempts to bounce back from Sunday's devastation.

articles.title: Bears' offense evaporates, Caleb Williams injured late in loss to Vikings
articles.summary: Caleb Williams left in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury, and the Bears dropped to 1-1.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears ' season took a dramatic and dark turn in Week 2.

Following a 59-point outing in Week 1, the Bears came crashing down in their Week 2 loss, 9-3 to the Vikings , as QB Caleb Williams suffered a non-contact right hamstring injury in the fourth quarter .

Williams, who had struggled most of the day, started to run on a first-and-goal play but went down without being touched and later was carted off the field.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson said after the game that Williams was in "good spirits" and was happy that Williams' injury was not his knee, but that the team wouldn't know the severity of it until further tests on Monday.

"Yeah, the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well, so we'll see," Johnson said. "We'll see how bad it is [Monday], but it's quickly you've got to turn the page — particularly when you're right there [near the end zone]. We needed the points pretty desperately at that point, and you know, it's a shame."

Tyson Bagent replaced Williams and couldn't convert on second or third down. Cairo Santos ' game-tying 23-yard field-goal attempt was then blocked. The Vikings drained more than five minutes of clock and tacked on the extra cushion with Will Reichard 's third field goal of the game.

Last week, the Bears and Vikings combined for 98 points. This weekend on a rainy, sloppy Soldier Field: four field goals.

"In between the trenches, I thought our guys answered the bell against a team we knew that wanted to run it," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said.

The Vikings are now 2-0, led by their ferocious defense. Minnesota blitzed Williams relentlessly early and often, creating havoc for the Bears. The Vikings had four sacks, including two from Dallas Turner .

The final play of the game was a beaut from Turner:

Carson Wentz stepped in to start for an injured Kyler Murray , playing turnover-free ball and delivering just enough big connections to secure the victory. The Vikings also received good production from Aaron Jones , who ran for 105 yards despite leaving the game with injury.

The Bears, who fell to 1-1, had their chances. Bagent led the Bears down on their last-gasp drive, but he was sacked on fourth down on the final play of the game by Turner, a fitting end in a dominant defensive showing from Minnesota and coordinator Brian Flores.

Williams finished the game 15-of-26 passing for 138 yards and an interception, also rushing for 42 yards on five runs. Bagent finished 5-of-9 passing for 54 yards.

Seven of the Bears' eight penalties were on offense, as center Garrett Bradbury was guilty of three of them (plus a fourth that offset a Vikings roughing-the-passer call). The Bears were guilty of three straight penalties, and four in a five-play span, that knocked them out of field-goal range and led to a punt late in the second quarter.

It was that kind of day for Chicago offensively. The Bears outgained the Vikings, 297 yards to 246, but couldn't convert on their scoring chances well enough.

articles.title: Bryce Young, Tyler Shough and Top Fantasy Waiver-Wire QBs After Caleb Williams Injury
articles.summary: Caleb Williams appeared to suffer major hamstring during Sunday's contest against the Minnesota Vikings, a huge concern for the Chicago Bears going forward.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams appeared to suffer major hamstring during Sunday's contest against the Minnesota Vikings, a huge concern for the Chicago Bears going forward.

Fantasy enthusiasts who rostered Williams may also need to start considering other options. Below we'll break down some of the players to have on your radar, including Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young and the New Orleans Saints Tyler Shough.

Young has come out hot to start the 2026 season, with three touchdown passes in each of his first two games (and a rushing touchdown in Week 1). He took a nice step forward in his third season last year and appears to be hitting another level yet again.

The talent is there—he was a top overall pick in 2023 for a reason. But now the fantasy results are starting to follow after three seasons of being an afterthought.

Whether this is sustainable remains to be seen, but if you are scouring waivers for help at quarterback you can only afford to be so choosy. Young should be a top consideration.

Shough has now exceeded 22 fantasy points in each of his first two games, leading the Saints to a win and a tight overtime loss. The Saints appear to have some real juice in the passing game, even if his fantasy totals on Sunday were propped up somewhat by a quarterback-sneak touchdown.

But 662 passing yards and five total touchdowns through two games is a good sign. If Shough is available in your league he's a fantastic pickup.

We're digging pretty deep here, given that 12 of Cam Ward's 20 fantasy points on Sunday came from a pair of rushing touchdowns. But for deeper or superflex leagues, you may not have much of a choice but to take a chance on a fringe player, and Ward's rushing ability gives him just enough upside to consider.

Young and Shough are much better options. But if neither are available, you may have to roll the dice on Ward's legs and hope his arm takes a jump as the season progresses.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel Sidesteps Struggles by Drake Maye, Patriots Offense After Win vs. Steelers
articles.summary: The New England Patriots picked up a win against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, but it wasn't because of a strong offensive showing.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots picked up a win against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, but it wasn't because of a strong offensive showing.

After the 20-3 win, head coach Mike Vrabel wasn't interested in criticizing quarterback Drake Maye and the offense.

"Just trying to win the game. You're not going to run my Sunday," Vrabel told reporters when asked about his level of concern with Maye and the offense.

Getting the win is what matters most, but there are certainly some concerns that Vrabel and his staff will want to address. Maye finished with just 208 passing yards and an interception on 14-of-22 passing. He also took three sacks and was hit seven times total.

Luckily for Vrabel and the Patriots, the Steelers managed just 278 yards of offense as New England's defense did its job. Aaron Rodgers threw an interception in the red zone, and the Pats forced a fumble that turned into a touchdown.

While the Patriots had enough to win on Sunday, that kind of offensive performance won't fly against the Jacksonville Jaguars next week or the Buffalo Bills the following week.

It wasn't a turnover fest for the Patriots' offense, but rather drives fizzling out earlier than they should have.

"Definitely not where we want to be," Maye told reporters. "I think it's just a point of making the plays, picking up the first downs and just stalling out. I think it starts with me making good decisions, good plays and it starts with us finishing the drives."

The Pats' offense was even worse in Week 1, albeit against a better defense. In a 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, Maye threw for just 178 yards and a touchdown, along with three interceptions, one of which sealed the win for the defending champions.

New England is hoping to get back to the Super Bowl this year, but its offense has looked far from a championship contender through the first two weeks of the season.

articles.title: Carolina Panthers win first game as favorite in nearly 5 years with rout of Atlanta Falcons
articles.summary: The Panthers won their first game as a favorite in nearly five years.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers haven't been a favorite very often in recent seasons, but they did close as a 2.5-point road favorite against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday.

Carolina not only hadn't covered any of its last 12 games as a favorite, but had lost all of them outright.

The last game the Panthers had won outright as a favorite came nearly five years ago, back on Sept. 23, 2021, when Carolina beat the Houston Texans 24-9 as a 4.5-point home favorite.

It was a different story Sunday afternoon.

The Panthers routed the Falcons 34-3 , as they led 10-0 after the first quarter and 20-3 at halftime. Falcons starting quarterback Cooper Rush went 10-of-17 for 86 yards and two interceptions, while Bryce Young threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns in the win. The Falcons had five turnovers, and the game was never truly in doubt.

Last season, Carolina was a favorite only twice — -2.5 at New Orleans in Week 15 and -5.5 vs. New Orleans in Week 10 — and lost both games outright.

The Panthers are at the Browns in Week 3.

articles.title: Tyler Shough scores on controversial sneak to stun Ravens in another fourth-quarter collapse
articles.summary: Tyler Shough once again found his stride late, this time leading the Saints to a victory.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens may have hired a new head coach in the offseason, but they looked a lot like the Ravens of old in Week 2. Despite leading 17-9 in the final quarter, the Ravens were stunned by the New Orleans Saints , who came back to win 24-17 on Sunday.

New Orleans scored 15 unanswered points in the game's final quarter, with quarterback Tyler Shough again finding his stride after a difficult start. With his team down multiple scores, Shough threw a 21-yard touchdown to Chris Olave and then scored a rushing touchdown with 1:30 left to put the Saints ahead for good.

That second touchdown was subject to controversy, as the refs determined Shough crossed the goal line on a sneak despite an unclear angle on replay.

"That was, uh, such an interesting play," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said. "… You know, those are so subjective, so hard to tell. It is what it is, honestly."

The Ravens had one more opportunity to tie or win the game. Lamar Jackson attempted to rally the team, but threw an interception with 20 seconds left to give the Saints the victory.

It marked the second straight week in which the Saints rallied after a poor first half. In Week 1, the team erased a 21-point deficit to eventually send the Detroit Lions to overtime. Despite Shough hitting some clutch throws in the comeback, the Saints ultimately fell in overtime after trying to go for the win with a late 2-point conversion. Shough's luck ran out on the game's final throw, as it sailed a little too deep out of the end zone, giving New Orleans a 31-30 loss , despite its late heroics.

This time around, Shough and the team pulled out the victory. It once again came after a quiet first half in which the Saints were limited to two field goals. Things remained quiet in the third quarter, as the Saints kicked yet another field goal.

The team finally rallied on its first drive in the fourth quarter, as Shough led a nine-play drive that ended in Olave's score. The Saints then went for 2 and converted on a Travis Etienne run to tie the game at 17.

After forcing a punt, Shough led the Saints down to the 1-yard line. The team attempted a sneak on third-and-goal, though Shough was ruled down at the 1. The team tried a sneak again on fourth down, this one deemed successful.

With the fourth-quarter rally, Shough finished the contest 27-of-34 for 252 passing yards and one passing touchdown. He rushed for 23 yards and a touchdown as well.

Ravens collapse again in the fourth quarter

While the Ravens were incredibly successful during the John Harbaugh era, the team developed a reputation for blowing leads in the fourth quarter. After 18 seasons with the Ravens, Harbaugh was let go in January in favor of Minter.

Minter was brought in to clean up some of those late-game issues and reinvigorate a Ravens offense that was good, but not great, last season.

In Week 1, it appeared Minter solved both issues. The Ravens dropped 41 points in a Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts . Baltimore scored 31 points in the first half, and limited the Colts to 10 points in the second half.

As impressive as that performance looked, the Ravens proved in Week 2 that they might not be fully over their old demons. Following Sunday's collapse, Baltimore will look to get back on track against the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro next weekend.

The Saints, meanwhile, will take on the Las Vegas Raiders after two encouraging games against tough opponents to open the 2026 NFL season.

Sunday's game between the Cleveland Browns and Tampa Bay Buccaneers has been delayed due to thunderstorms in Tampa, leaving a soggy field in its wake.

articles.title: Drew Lock finds a wide-open Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a perfect 82-yard TD early vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Drew Lock seems to be handling his new starting role in Seattle just fine.
articles.body:
Drew Lock seems to be handling his new starting role in Seattle just fine.

The Seahawks quarterback threw a perfect 82-yard touchdown pass to All-Pro wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba on his very first pass of the game in their matchup with the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. That put Seattle up 7-0 almost instantly at State Farm Stadium.

That marked the longest touchdown reception of Smith-Njigba's career. The Cardinals did little to stop him, either, and left him completely open along the right sideline for the easy score. All Smith-Njigba had to do was juke briefly, and he was past cornerback Will Johnson and safety Budda Baker into open field.

Smith-Njigba has now scored twice this season. He caught a 45-yard touchdown pass from Lock in the fourth quarter of their 13-10 comeback win over the New England Patriots to open the NFL season. Lock stepped in to replace Sam Darnold, who went down early with a hip injury.

The Seahawks said that Darnold has a "very unique soft-tissue injury," and they don't expect him to be sidelined for long. He was not active for Sunday's game in Arizona, but head coach Mike Macdonald said that they don't expect him to land "on IR or anything like that." It seems like Darnold will be back sooner rather than later, though a specific timeline isn't yet known.

In the meantime, Lock is doing just fine leading the way.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts saves Eagles from ugly upset as Philadelphia escapes Titans to remain unbeaten
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts hit Darius Cooper for a last-second touchdown to erase a three-point deficit as the Philadelphia Eagles escaped Nashville 24-20.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles moved to 2-0 with a win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon in Nashville. That's a sentence most football fans expected to read before the game even started. What most probably didn't expect was exactly what it took for the Eagles to go into Nissan Stadium and beat the Titans. Jalen Hurts connected with Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with less than 10 seconds remaining to turn a 20-17 Tennessee lead into a 24-20 Philadelphia victory. articles.title: Tyler Shough Reveals Saints Coaches Called Him 'Poor Man' After Ravens DC's Josh Allen Comments
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints coaching staff used a slight from Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver to motivate their quarterback this week.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints coaching staff used a slight from Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver to motivate their quarterback this week.

Weaver called Tyler Shough a "poor man's Josh Allen" earlier this week, so the coaching staff referred to him as "poor man" all week.

Shough and the Saints ultimately got the last laugh, though, beating the Ravens 24-17 in an upset victory.

Shough, who is in his second season, threw for 252 yards and a touchdown in the win.

articles.title: Packers WR Jayden Reed staying in New York overnight with neck injury, has movement in his extremities; RT Zach Bako-Bewele 'could be out for a long time'
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed left the field on a cart with his head stabilized after a frightening scene during Sunday's game against the New...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Jayden Reed left the field on a cart with his head stabilized after a frightening scene during Sunday's overtime victory against the New York Jets .

The Packers quickly ruled him out with a neck injury.

Packers right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele also left in the first quarter with a knee injury and was ruled out. The Packers rallied from a 17-7 fourth-quarter deficit for a 20-17 win in overtime.

After the game, head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Reed would remain in New York overnight, but that he had movement in all of his extremities.

"He's got movement in all his extremities," LaFleur said in his postgame news conference. "He will be staying overnight. That was obviously a very scary deal any time you see anybody down on the field and have to get carted off."

LaFleur didn't offer details on the nature of Reed's injury. Reed, meanwhile, offered an encouraging update of his own on social media.

LaFleur also said that Bako-Bewele's injury "doesn't look good either."

"He could be out for a long time," LaFleur said, without noting the precise nature of Bako-Bewele's knee injury.

Reed carted off after being placed on backboard

Jets linebacker Demario Davis made contact to Reed's head with his shoulder pad on a hit in the first quarter. Reed was face down on the ground for a moment before rolling over to his back.

Medical staff immediately tended to Reed, and Packers players left their bench to surround their injured teammate as a cart came out.

Trainers put Reed on a backboard and stabilized his head before placing him on a cart. Reed was then taken off the field on the cart.

Reed, 26, is a fourth-year pro who's played his entire career for the Packers since being selected in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He's the No. 2 receiver on Green Bay 's depth chart behind Christian Watson .

Collarbone and foot injuries limited Reed to seven games in 2025. In his last full NFL season in 2024, Reed tallied 55 catches for 857 yards and 6 touchdowns. He posted three catches for 20 yards in Green Bay's Week 1 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .

articles.title: Robert Griffin III Makes Pitch for Falcons Contract with Rush, Strand 'Stinking It Up'

How bad is the quarterback situation in Atlanta at the moment?

Robert Griffin III believes the Falcons would be better off utilizing a number of older players who haven't played in years—like himself, Cam Newton and Ryan Tannehill—rather than trot out Cooper Rush and Jack Strand:

That he may have point is a testament to just how bad the quarterback play has been in Atlanta. articles.title: Atlanta Falcons are dealing with the worst quarterback situation in the NFL and it isn't even close
articles.summary: Cooper Rush fumbled and threw two interceptions before Kevin Stefanski benched him, and his replacement threw a pick six in his Falcons debut.
articles.body: The worst quarterback situation in the NFL right now? The Atlanta Falcons. And it isn't very close at all. FALCONS QUARTERBACK PROBLEMS DEEPEN AS TUA TAGOVAILOA SUFFERS OBLIQUE STRAIN AT PRACTICE And Tagovailoa was out for the second consecutive week after he suffered an unexpected oblique injury two weeks ago, this time in practice. articles.title: Drake London Says Fan Got 'Personal' During Verbal Confrontation in Falcons' 34-3 Loss to Panthers
articles.summary: Drake London went back and forth with a fan during the Atlanta Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, and the wide receiver said after the game that the fan made things "personal."
articles.body:
Drake London went back and forth with a fan during the Atlanta Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, and the wide receiver said after the game that the fan made things "personal."

"I'm going to be honest here, I don't take light to disrespect at all," London told reporters . "I don't care who you are. I'm a man, too, at the end of the day. So, if you want to get on a personal level, I can get there, too, but it's not the right thing to do. So, I got to take accountability for that, and I got to push forward and be the bigger man in some of those situations."

During the third quarter of the frustrating loss to a divisional rival, London was seen shouting profanities at a fan inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium as his teammate, Olamide Zaccheaus, held him back.

London admitted that responding to the fan was "not the right thing to do."

London had a frustrating start to the season when he recorded just two receptions for 29 yards in Week 1, and it didn't get much better in Week 2. He finished Sunday's game with four receptions for 51 yards.

"I think we as playmakers—us in the backfield, us on the outside, on the wing—we got to go out there and make plays regardless," London said. "We're all in the league for a reason, right? We're all good football players. I don't care if you're fourth string or you're the starter."

The fan London got into it with wasn't the only one who was frustrated with the Falcons' performance. Despite it being a home game, fans in the stadium started booing as things got out of hand.

"To me, it just gives me more juice to go out there and prove everybody wrong," London told reporters . "If we have everybody against us, then all you can do is push forward if your back's against the wall."

The Falcons are still awaiting the return of quarterbacks Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa. Cooper Rush started for Atlanta and threw for 86 yards and two interceptions, and he was replaced by Jack Strand, who threw for 59 yards and an interception.

Atlanta has had a frustrating start to the season, and those frustrations clearly boiled over on Sunday.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Calls Out Jeffery Simmons' Comments About QB on Video After Eagles Beat Titans
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts kept the receipts.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback had some friendly banter for Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons after leading a game-winning touchdown drive during Sunday's 24-20 victory.

"We just need to make Jalen Hurts be a quarterback," Simmons told reporters this week. "Stop his runs, make sure Hurts doesn't get out of the pocket and make plays."

Given the seemingly never-ending debate about Hurts as a quarterback, those comments quickly made the rounds.

As a pure passer, Hurts isn't elite. He's never thrown for 4,000 yards or 30 touchdowns in a season. But the conversation shouldn't stop there—you also have to consider his ability to make plays with his legs; his ability to limit turnovers and manage the game; his tendency to make plays in the clutch and deliver on the biggest stage (one Super Bowl title, two excellent Super Bowl performances); and the fact that he just wins, year in and year out, despite Philadelphia's revolving door of offensive coordinators.

Much of that was displayed on Philly's final drive Sunday, when Hurts led a nine-play, 65-yard drive in under two minutes, resulting in Darius Cooper's game-winning touchdown reception.

Hurts wasn't perfect on Sunday, throwing two interceptions. But as usual, he had the last word.

articles.title: James Harrison, Le'Veon Bell Rip Steelers in Trending Posts After Blowout Loss to Patriots
articles.summary: Several former Pittsburgh Steelers players are not happy with the state of the team.
articles.body:
Several former Pittsburgh Steelers players are not happy with the state of the team.

After the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on Sunday, James Harrison and Le'Veon Bell called them out on social media.

Harrison called the team "cooked" and ripped the offensive line, while Bell called out wide receiver DK Metcalf, as well as the defense as a whole.

Steelers fans are likely on the same page as Harrison and Bell after what transpired on Sunday.

Pittsburgh's offense looked dreadful against the defending AFC champions, mustering just 278 yards of total offense. Aaron Rodgers threw for 187 yards and an interception, and he also had a fumble that resulted in a New England touchdown.

Metcalf did very little in the loss, hauling in four receptions for just 27 yards. The ground game couldn't get going either, with just 91 rushing yards from the group.

To be fair to Pittsburgh, its defense didn't look all that lost as it held Drake Maye to just 208 yards, picking up one interception. The Patriots' offense also had just 13 points, since one of New England's touchdowns came on defense.

The Steelers picked up a win in Week 1 against the Atlanta Falcons, but they looked far from a playoff contender in the loss on Sunday. Things also won't get much easier next week as they face the Cincinnati Bengals.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Injured, Latest on Commanders Star's Timeline to Return After Exiting vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered another early-season injury in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys and was ruled out of the game.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered another early-season injury in Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys and was ruled out of the game.

Daniels suffered an elbow injury right before halftime while the Commanders were on the Cowboys' goal line. Clarence Hill Jr. of All City DLLS reported that he had to be carted off the field.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said after the game that Daniels had dislocated his elbow and would undergo further testing on Monday.

Daniels later left the stadium with a sling:

When Fox analyst Tom Brady saw a replay of the injury, he said on the live broadcast, "Oh s--t. Excuse me. Was not expecting to see that."

Washington ultimately fell 37-20 without Daniels.

Daniels dealt with a difficult 2025 season that saw him play just seven games due to injury.

In Week 2 , Daniels suffered a left knee sprain against the Green Bay Packers. He finished the game but missed the next two weeks.

In Week 7 , Daniels sustained a right hamstring injury in a third quarter his team's matchup with the Dallas Cowboys. He left the game, got ruled out and missed one more week.

In Week 9 , Daniels suffered a scary injury when he was sacked and got his left arm twisted in the wrong direction during a game against the Seattle Seahawks. Thankfully, an ailment that appeared to be far worse at first turned out to be a dislocated left elbow. The injury was still serious, of course, but he returned after missing three games.

Unfortunately, in Week 14 at the Minnesota Vikings, Daniels suffered a re-aggravation of the left elbow injury.

He sat the team's next game at the New York Giants on Dec. 14. One day later, the Commanders decided to rule him out for their final three games.

For the season, Daniels completed 60.6 percent of his passes for 1,262 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions while adding 278 rushing yards and two scores.

It was a tough year for Daniels, but as he's shown, the 2023 Heisman Trophy winner is capable of greatness. In his rookie season, Daniels led the Commanders to 14 wins (including playoffs) and the team's first NFC Championship Game appearance since 1991. During the regular season, he accounted for 31 total touchdowns (25 passing, six rushing) and 4,459 total yards (891 rushing).

Without Daniels, the Commanders will turn to Marcus Mariota. The former Oregon star and 11-year veteran, who the Tennessee Titans selected second in the 2015 NFL draft, has previously performed admirably in Daniels' absence.

articles.summary: Jayden Daniels missed 10 games last season due to injury.
articles.body:
The end of the first half ended horribly for the Washington Commanders , and not because of a failed play near the goal line.

On the final play of the first half against the Dallas Cowboys , Jayden Daniels was stepped on as he took a snap, stumbled to the ground and was in pain afterward. He appeared to injure his elbow when he braced himself after he was tripped, and it looked similar to his dislocated left elbow he suffered last season.

Daniels was carted off the field as the teams were back in the locker room for halftime.

The dislocated elbow caused Daniels to miss four games last season, and then in his first game back he re-injured it and didn't play again the rest of the season.

Daniels had a historic rookie season for the Commanders but played in just seven games last season due to injuries. Most of the time he missed was due to the injured elbow. While the Commanders will hope for the best, Sunday's injury was a frightening reminder of what happend last season.

articles.title: Patriots get devastating injury update on longtime offensive lineman
articles.summary: Patriots veteran offensive lineman Mike Onwenu is reportedly feared to have suffered a season-ending injury in Sunday's win over the Steelers.
articles.body:
There are reportedly concerns that New England Patriots longtime offensive lineman Mike Onwenu might miss the rest of the season with the leg injury that he suffered in the Week 2 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers .

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the news after the game on Sunday.

Onwenu was carted off the field after the gruesome injury, which was a result of getting his leg rolled up under a Steelers defender. It looked like a serious injury from the visual eye alone, but the Patriots will know more once medical imaging is done.

But the early tests have seemingly not been good.

Onwenu is arguably the Patriots' best offensive lineman. He has long been one of the best guards in the NFL, and his potential absence creates a serious void at the position. With Onwenu out, the Patriots will likely turn to veteran Greg Van Roten to step up as the new starter.

The good news is that Van Roten has plenty of starting experience in the NFL. So they won't be sacrificing experience with the change. But if Onwenu really is out for the season, it will be hard to replace the talent and security that he brought to the position on a weekly basis.

articles.title: Jets collapse late against Packers, miss chance at first 2-0 start since 2015 in overtime loss
articles.summary: The New York Jets blew a 17-7 fourth quarter lead as the Green Bay Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime at MetLife Stadium.
articles.body: For most of Sunday afternoon, the New York Jets looked poised to move to 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets controlled most of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, but made some crucial errors down the stretch to cough up their 10-point fourth-quarter lead. The Packers scored 13 unanswered points to win 20-17 in overtime, with Trey Smack kicking a 26-yard field goal to complete the comeback. Green Bay struck first on a 6-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to MarShawn Lloyd in the second quarter, but the Jets answered with a 5-yard touchdown run from Braelon Allen. Geno Smith connected with Garrett Wilson for a 5-yard score in the third quarter to give New York a 14-7 lead. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Jets appeared to have delivered the knockout blow early in the fourth quarter when they recovered a Lloyd fumble at the Green Bay 18-yard line. But the offense couldn't move the ball and settled for a 32-yard Jason Sanders field goal, extending the lead to 17-7 with 11:04 remaining. That's when everything started to unravel. A 38-yard pass-interference penalty helped Green Bay march down the field before Love found Christian Watson for a 3-yard touchdown. The Jets failed to pick up a first down on their next possession, and Skyy Moore returned the ensuing punt 63 yards to the New York 19-yard line. Smack kicked a 34-yard field goal four plays later to tie the game. New York still had a chance to win in regulation. After Breece Hall gained just one yard on third-and-2, the Jets faced fourth-and-1 at midfield with 1:20 remaining. Aaron Glenn kept his offense on the field rather than punting, an aggressive decision to try to win the game. It's hard to fault Glenn for trusting his offense to gain one yard, but Braelon Allen was stuffed. Green Bay failed to capitalize, sending the game to overtime. The Jets received the ball first in overtime and the possession was a complete disaster. The Packers sacked Smith on consecutive plays, the offense committed a false-start penalty and New York faced a third-and-30 from their own 10-yard line before eventually punting on fourth down. Green Bay then moved 58 yards on four offensive plays, aided by an unnecessary roughness penalty against Jarvis Brownlee Jr., before Smack ended the game on the fifth play of the drive. But the timing of the Jets' two biggest penalties proved especially costly: the 38-yard pass-interference call aided Green Bay's fourth-quarter touchdown drive, while Brownlee's 15-yard penalty moved the Packers into position for the winning field goal. Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. It wasn't a spectacular performance, but it should have been good enough given how well New York's defense played.
