articles.title: Aaron Rodgers acknowledges Steelers offense isn't playing 'winning football' after listless effort in loss to Patriots
articles.summary: For the second time in two 2026 games, Drake Maye wasn't great. On Sunday, he didn't need to be. New England's defense teed off on Aaron Rodgers and an impot...
articles.body:
For the second time in two 2026 games, Drake Maye wasn't great. On Sunday, he didn't need to be.

New England 's defense teed off on Aaron Rodgers and an impotent Pittsburgh Steelers offense to lead a 20-3 Patriots win.

The Patriots forced two fumbles from the 42-year-old Steelers quarterback. One of them resulted in a 36-yard loss and a fourth-and-43 punt. The second resulted in a scoop-and-score touchdown that extended New England's lead to 20-3 and iced the win.

New England then ended Pittsburgh's best chance of scoring a touchdown with an interception of Rodgers that abruptly ended a 72-yard fourth-quarter drive.

When Rodgers wasn't getting hit or turning the ball over, he faced consistent pressure and struggled to move Pittsburgh's offense in any meaningful way.

Aaron Rodgers: Offense isn't playing 'winning football'

After the game, Rodgers acknowledged that the Steelers' offense wasn't pulling its weight. The unit accounted for 13 points in Week 1's 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in which a T.J. Watt pick 6 accounted for the difference in the game.

"Defense has been playing great, they've been holding 13 points a game in two games," Rodgers told reporters . "I think offensively, we're averaging, like eight points a game. It's not winning football. … When they hold them to 13 points, we've got to win the game."

Rodgers said that it was up to offensive players to "play better" and "give a little more" and that "it starts with me." He also said that he and head coach Mike McCarthy wouldn't react by panicking.

"You're not gonna see me panic," Rodgers continued. "I don't think Mike's gonna panic. Urgency's gonna go up a little bit, for sure. But no panic."

Rodgers completed 23-of-39 passes for 187 yards (4.8 yards per attempt) with no touchdowns and an interception. He took four sacks and was hit seven other times. He and former Pro Bowl receiver DK Metcalf struggled to connect as Metcalf finished with 4 catches for 27 yards.

No Steelers receiver talled more than 35 yards through the air. Pittsburgh's offense managed 235 yards on 3.5 yards per play.

The Patriots struck first on Sunday with a 39-yard first-quarter touchdown run from TreVeyon Henderson in his first game of the season after missing Week 1 with an ankle injury. That turned out to be all the points New England needed to secure the win.

With the Patriots holding a 10-0 lead in the second quarter, Pittsburgh had a shot to get on the board with third-and-7 at New England's 22-yard line. But Christian Elliss sacked Rodgers and forced a fumble, setting off a mad scramble as the ball bounced back toward the Pittsburgh end zone .

Steelers tackle Troy Fautanu eventually recovered the ball, but the 36-yard loss doomed Pittsburgh's scoring chance and forced a punt on the next play.

Then in the fourth quarter, the Patriots forced Rodgers' second fumble of the day, this time in Steelers territory. Christian Barmore got pressure up the middle and forced the ball loose. Elijah Ponder scooped it up and returned the ball 19 yards for a touchdown.

Two possessions later, Pittsburgh responded with what looked liked its best drive of the game in a late effort to make things competitive.

But wide receiver Germie Bernard failed to catch a screen pass in the red zone. Instead, he bobbled it in the air, allowing linebacker Gabe Jacas to intercept it and effectively end the game.

The effort capped an overwhelming effort from New England's defense that got the Patriots back on the right track after they blew a 10-0 second half lead in Week 1's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks .

After throwing three second-half interceptions in that loss to Seattle, Maye was far from perfect on Sunday. He threw another ill-advised pass that resulted in an interception on an underthrown downfield look to Hunter Henry that Patrick Queen picked off.

The interception with New England holding a 10-3 lead momentarily allowed the Steelers to stay in the game.

But Maye was good enough in keeping the Patriots' offense functional as their defense set the tone for the win. Maye finished his day completing 14-of-22 passes for 208 yards with no touchdowns and an interception.

Henderson paced New England's offense with 76 rushing yards and the unit's only touchdown on 16 carries.

The Patriots (1-1) will take the win and hope for a more balanced effort in Week 3 in what projects as a difficult matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

The Steelers (1-1) move on to face the high-octane Cincinnati Bengals in search of an offensive fix that won't be easy to find.

articles.body:
There's more good news regarding the right hamstring injury suffered by Bears quarterback Caleb Williams on Sunday.

Via Adam Jahns of CHGO_Sports, Williams (who didn't speak to reporters after the game) came through the locker room with media present. Per the report, Williams "was walking under his own power, no crutches or anything, maybe a slight limp."

He's in "good spirits," we're told, about attacking the recovery process.

Bears coach Ben Johnson said after the game that they will know more about the injury on Monday, when Williams has an MRI.

The Bears host the Eagles next Monday night.

articles.title: Tom Brady slips on air after seeing replay of Jayden Daniels' gruesome elbow injury vs. Cowboys: 'Oh s***'
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels' left elbow bent back awkwardly on the final play before halftime on Sunday afternoon, and he had to be carted off the field.
articles.body:
Tom Brady was just like the rest of us after seeing Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels go down late in the first half of their game with the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday afternoon.

Brady, calling the game on Fox, was left stunned by the replay that showed Daniels' elbow bend awkwardly out of place at AT&T Stadium.

While it may have been among the most relatable things Brady has ever done, he quickly apologized for his gaffe.

"Excuse me," he said. "Was not expecting to see that."

Daniels was stepped on as he took a snap near the Cowboys' goal line right before halftime, and he stumbled to the ground. As he was going down, he braced himself with his arm. The injury looked similar to the dislocated left elbow he suffered last season.

Specifics aren't known, but Daniels was carted off the field to the locker room as the two teams went back for halftime. The Commanders ruled him out with a left elbow injury soon after.

The injury was the second significant one in the final sequence. Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant was stepped on by teammate Markquese Bell in several spots that you do not want to be stepped on. RedZone's Scott Hanson had the unique call on that one.

Durant ended up walking back to the locker room early. He was ruled out with a hamstring injury.

Brady signed a massive 10-year deal to become Fox Sports' lead analyst alongside Kevin Burkhardt after his playing career ended. He's only in the third season with Fox, but fully plans to be with the network through the deal.

"I have a lot to prove to myself, to my teammates. I have a lot to prove to the executives," Brady said earlier this month, via the Sports Business Journal . "I want to go earn it and I don't want anything given to me. I hope they'll have me through the end of this contract."

While his expletive on Sunday may not have been the most professional, it's easy to understand why it slipped out. The replay of Daniels' injury was brutal.

articles.title: NFL Week 2 Winners and Losers: Deshaun Watson has his best moment for Browns in win, likely keeps job for another week
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson came into Sunday's game needing a big performance.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns waited a long time for some positive vibes on Deshaun Watson . Then they waited some more.

The Browns, led by two Watson touchdown passes in the second half, beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 23-19. They clinched the win after a delay for lightning that lasted about two hours. For Watson, it was worth the wait.

Sunday was likely his greatest moment with the Browns, not that there are many to choose from. It also probably saved his job for at least another week.

The consensus thought was that Watson would get the first two games to start for the Browns, and after he struggled, he'd be replaced before Cleveland's fans could boo him relentlessly in the home opener. Watson could, of course, keep his job with a good performance. He needed it going into the game.

Watson wasn't good in the opener. He threw a bad interception right away in that game. The only time the Browns scored a touchdown was late in the game when they trailed by 31. Watson made a tone-deaf comment during the week that he thought the media expected him to throw for 400 yards and five touchdowns every week. That wasn't exactly true. Competence was a reasonable expectation, though.

The first half Sunday wasn't a fantastic start, either. In the first half against a Buccaneers defense that isn't exactly great, the Browns had 59 yards on 25 plays. Watson wasn't making any horrific mistakes, but he wasn't making much happen, either. It seemed like he was two quarters from definitely losing his job. When Watson did make a nice throw in the third quarter, he didn't get much help, as his throw to Denzel Boston in the end zone was juggled and dropped.

Boston helped him later, taking a short catch, breaking through three tackles and going for a 55-yard touchdown and a tie game. That started a rally for the Browns, and Watson. It's possible the rest of the game was be the difference in him starting another game or more, or being benched.

The Buccaneers took the lead after the Boston touchdown, but Watson led a go-ahead drive. He hit Blake Whiteheart on a 17-yard touchdown for a 23-19 lead.

Then there was a twist. The Buccaneers were at the Browns' 28-yard line at the two-minute warning when the weather caused some chaos. The game was suspended due to lightning. The late afternoon games were already at halftime or in the second half, and the Browns and Buccaneers waited in the locker room for an important final two minutes. It had some extra importance for Watson.

The game resumed at 6:10 p.m. Eastern, with the rain still pouring down. The Buccaneers quickly picked up a first down, but were then pushed back 10 yards due to a holding penalty. Ted Hurst III had a catchable pass in the end zone after that but he couldn't bring it in. Baker Mayfield threw incomplete on fourth down, and the Browns had the win.

The Browns needed the win, and nobody more than Watson. He threw for 238 yards and two touchdowns, and led the team with 22 yards rushing. There haven't been many positive moments like that for him in Cleveland. Since his trade from the Houston Texans , he has mostly been awful. His contract has been called one of the worst in NFL history, and the trade for him has been called one of the worst in NFL history. He got a bit of redemption on Sunday.

Watson presumably will keep his job for another week. We'll see what reaction Browns fans have for him.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 2 of the NFL season:

Brian Flores: One of these days, Flores might get another shot to be a head coach.

The Chicago Bears put up 59 points last week, and though rain was a factor Sunday, so was Flores' defense. The Bears did practically nothing on offense in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings . It was a painful day for Chicago in many ways, as the Bears saw Caleb Williams get carted off due to an injury . But that mishap came late in the fourth quarter, so it's not like that was the main reason the Bears ' offense wasn't good. It could have a huge impact on Chicago's season, though.

The Bears were driving when Williams was injured and were about to tie the game on a short field goal, but it was blocked. In the final seconds, with the Bears at Minnesota 's 12-yard line, Williams' replacement, Tyson Bagent , was sacked, and the Vikings improved to 2-0.

Minnesota's offense with Carson Wentz at quarterback wasn't very good, but it didn't matter much. Flores, who filed a racial discrimination lawsuit against the NFL and could have that working against him as he seeks another head-coaching job, is having another great season coordinating the Vikings' defense. That will lead to more head-coaching interviews. Perhaps a team will actually hire him this time.

Kellen Moore and Tyler Shough : Like last week, the New Orleans Saints started slowly and then rallied. This time, they finished the job.

The Saints fell short in overtime at Detroit last week, when a two-point conversion was incomplete. On Sunday, they pulled off a big upset, beating the Baltimore Ravens 24-17. Shough brought the team back from a 17-9 deficit in the second half and scored the go-ahead touchdown on a fourth-and-inches quarterback sneak in the final two minutes. The Saints picked off Lamar Jackson after that and had the win. Shough had 252 yards and a touchdown passing and 23 yards and the game-winning touchdown rushing.

Moore, the Saints' second-year head coach, and Shough were each impressive last season, as they got hot in the second half after Shough took over as the starting quarterback. The Saints had two tough road games to start this season. They came out of it 1-1 and were one play from a 2-0 start. The Saints are already showing their good finish to last season wasn't a fluke.

Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals ' defense: Chase was quiet in Week 1 with two catches for 12 yards. Everyone knew that wouldn't continue.

Chase had two touchdowns Sunday in a 20-6 win over the Houston Texans. Those were the only touchdowns of the game. The first TD was a magnificent play that only a few receivers could make, as Chase twisted his body and hauled in a pass for the score as he tumbled to the ground.

A big part of the win was the Bengals' defense, which is showing it is much improved last season. The biggest difference is defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II, acquired in an offseason trade with the Giants for the 10th overall pick of the draft. Lawrence had a dominant day, and made one of the biggest plays of the game when he single-handedly beat a block and stopped David Montgomery cold on a fourth-and-inches run in the second quarter.

The Bengals' offense is going to be good. Chase is a great player and Joe Burrow can get him the ball. Cincinnati 's defense has been a question. It looks a lot better so far, and Lawrence has a lot to do with that. It caught a break facing a Texans team without its top receiver Nico Collins , but holding the Texans out of the end zone was a great sign going forward.

Jalen Hurts : The Philadelphia Eagles won't be thrilled to barely beat the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. The offense still has some issues to work out.

But a loss would have been much worse, and Hurts wouldn't let that happen.

The Titans took a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left, giving Hurts one last chance to save what would have been a bad loss. Hurts moved the Eagles downfield and hit Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with nine seconds left, and Philadelphia won 24-20. Cooper had nine catches and no touchdowns in his NFL career before Sunday. He has a pretty good highlight on his resume now. Hurts completed 6-of-8 passes on the final drive for 61 yards.

The Eagles saw Saquon Barkley limited due to a shoulder stinger he suffered early. He had nine rushing yards on just four carries. Hurts wasn't great as most of the offensive load fell on his shoulders. He threw two interceptions that almost cost the Eagles the game; the Titans got 10 points off those picks. But Hurts was good when he had to be. The Eagles are 2-0 with two last-minute wins against teams they were big favorites to beat, but being undefeated will help quiet at least some of the noise.

Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers : The Steelers were probably lucky to be facing the Falcons in Week 1.

Last week, the Steelers squeezed out a home win over a bad Falcons team. It wasn't an impressive performance. Had they been playing someone better, it probably would have been a loss. Sunday seemed like a more accurate representation of this season's Steelers. The New England Patriots beat the Steelers 20-3. It was a pretty easy day for the Patriots.

Aaron Rodgers in particular had a rough game. When he fumbled on a sack and the Patriots returned it for a touchdown, the score was 20-3 and the Pittsburgh offense wasn't coming back from that. Rodgers was 23 of 39 for 187 yards. For some reason the Steelers are building a pass-heavy attack around Rodgers, and it's not working so far.

Watching the Steelers the first two weeks is a reminder that their offseason plan was to settle on bringing back a quarterback who will be 43 years old in December. Pittsburgh's offense has looked bad through two weeks and they've yet to play a great defense. It might not get much better this season.

Kevin Stefanski: When Stefanski took the Atlanta Falcons job, it looked like a roster that was in decent shape other than a shaky quarterback situation. That should have been familiar from Stefanski's time with the Browns.

It turned out the quarterback situation in Atlanta was a complete debacle, which isn't too different than Stefanski's time with the Browns. On each of the Falcons' first two possessions Sunday, Cooper Rush turned the ball over. First it was a fumble, then an interception. After another interception, the Falcons put in undrafted rookie Jack Strand. The fans were chanting for the undrafted rookie and gave him an ovation when he came in, which speaks to the state of the team right now. Strand immediately threw a pick-6 to linebacker Devin Lloyd on a deflected pass. The Falcons are unwatchable right now on offense, and lost 34-3 to the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young continued a strong start to the season with 287 yards and three touchdowns, two of which went to Darren Waller .

It has to be some bad deja vu for Stefanski. At some point the Falcons will get Michael Penix Jr. back and while he'll be unquestionably better than Rush, he's probably not a savior either. The Falcons are an ugly 0-2 and unless Penix is much improved from last season when he returns there's not a lot of hope. That's not what Stefanski was hoping for.

Aaron Glenn: The New York Jets were on the verge of a 2-0 start to the season. But they couldn't finish.

Glenn came into the season on the hot seat, and losses like Sunday won't work in his favor. The Packers came back from a 10-point fourth quarter deficit and won 20-17 in overtime after New York's offense failed to do anything on its first possession. The Jets had plenty of opportunities to win and let it get away.

The Jets led 17-7 early in the fourth quarter but the Packers got back in the game. Christian Watson caught a 3-yard touchdown and a field goal after that tied the game. The Packers couldn't take advantage when the Jets were stopped on fourth down near midfield and the game went to overtime. That drive included Glenn not calling a timeout to conserve time with the Packers facing fourth-and-five at the Jets' 45. The Packers bluffed, took a delay of game and punted with 21 seconds left. Had the Jets taken a timeout and the Packers still punted, they would have had about 50 seconds and a timeout, needing a field goal to win in regulation.

On the first possession of overtime, Jets quarterback Geno Smith took a sack and that led to a punt. An unsportsmanlike penalty against the Jets on Green Bay 's first drive practically gave the Packers the win. Matthew Golden picked up 14 yards and Trey Smack came on for the game-winning field goal. It was a big escape for the Packers, who were in danger of going 0-2. It was a tough loss for the Jets and Glenn, who needs a good season to save his job.

articles.title: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels leaves game vs. Cowboys with elbow injury
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was ruled out of his team’s Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys after suffering an elbow injury late in the first half.
articles.body: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was ruled out of his team’s Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys after suffering an elbow injury late in the first half. With the Commanders one yard from the end zone and just three seconds remaining before halftime, Washington opted against kicking a field goal while trailing 17-10 and instead ran a play with Daniels under center. Daniels stumbled while dropping back to pass and reached out with his left hand in an attempt to steady himself, but his elbow popped out of place as he awkwardly reached for the ground. Daniels was carted off the field and underwent X-rays, according to the FOX broadcast. Daniels had completed 11 of his 17 passes against Dallas for 96 yards and a touchdown and added 69 yards on the ground before the injury. He was replaced by backup Marcus Mariota. The 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, Daniels suffered multiple injuries during a difficult second professional season in 2025, including a previous elbow injury that sidelined him four games. Daniels missed 10 games overall last season. He entered his third season healthy and looking for a bounce-back campaign, though Washington lost its season opener to Philadelphia.

articles.title: Browns Beat Bucs After Weather Delay, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Watson, Baker, Top Players
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns had to wait almost two extra hours to confirm their first win of the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns had to wait almost two extra hours to confirm their first win of the 2026 NFL regular season.

Cleveland defeated Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-19, in a game that was delayed just under two hours due to inclement weather in Tampa.

Watson and the Cleveland offense didn't come alive until the second half.

The Browns were down 16-6 in the third quarter before Watson ignited the come-from-behind effort.

Watson hit rookie Denzel Boston for a 55-yard touchdown pass that tied the game and swung the momentum fully in the Browns' favor.

Watson threw what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown pass to Blake Whiteheart with 3:51 left in the fourth quarter.

The former Houston Texans quarterback threw for 238 yards in one of his better games in a Browns uniform.

Mayfield struggled for most of the contest with only 182 passing yards. He only completed 61.8 percent of his passes and had a handful of overthrows, including one on the closing drive.

Mayfield's only touchdown pass of the game was a five-yard delivery to Emeka Egbuka at the start of the third quarter.

Instead of finding his stride in the second half, Mayfield continued to struggle and allowed the Browns to work their way back into the game behind Watson.

Watson and the Browns are now headed back home for three contests at home in their next four, starting with a Week 3 clash versus the Carolina Panthers. Tampa Bay hosts the Minnesota Vikings next Sunday.

During the play, Daniels seemed to hyperextend the left elbow. And, yes, it was ugly. It happened on the final play of the first half when Daniels pulled away from center but tripped. As he tried to regain his balance, he used his left arm to hold himself up. But X-rays showed no fracture. But it is clear that even after an MRI test on Monday, Daniels will miss time. Marcus Mariota will take the reins at quarterback until Daniels can return. "We will rally so hard around Marcus until, you know, Jayden's back," Quinn said. And all this is terrible news because Daniels had a similar injury in 2025 against the Seattle Seahawks. So this very easily could be a season-defining injury for Daniels. And the Commanders. Again. Although the injury was to his arm, Daniels was carted off to the locker room. He wore a towel over his head, apparently, to avoid showing his facial reaction to the crowd. An MRI found no fracture or ligament damage, so he avoided surgery and was not placed on injured reserve. The Commanders managed a 2-6 record in games Mariota started in place of Daniels last season, and they didn't rally to win on Sunday. articles.title: Watch Taylor Swift Show Off Wedding Ring in Viral Video to Celebrate Travis Kelce TD in Chiefs-Colts
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce spent his offseason celebrating his wedding with pop star Taylor Swift, but the veteran tight end hasn't missed a beat early this season.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce spent his offseason celebrating his wedding with pop star Taylor Swift, but the veteran tight end hasn't missed a beat early this season.

After a strong performance in Week 1, Kelce notched his first score of the year on a 13-yard pass from Patrick Mahomes. Swift celebrated accordingly, pointing to her wedding ring from her suite at Arrowhead Stadium.

Kelce weighed retirement this offseason, but so far, he looks like he's primed for another big season. That means Swift should have plenty to celebrate throughout the campaign.
